image_description: A close-up, low-light shot of a translucent blue disposable lighter against a black background. The lighter is ignited, producing a bright yellow-orange flame from the top right nozzle. The body appears to be made of semi-transparent plastic, revealing the internal fuel level or structure. The metal wind guard and ignition wheel assembly are visible at the top.

artifact_observations.reasoning: The surface of the blue plastic lacks fine micro-texture or molding lines expected in mass-produced plastic. It appears overly smooth and slightly 'waxy' or digitally blurred, lacking the crisp specular highlights of real hard plastic.

The connection between the flame and the metal nozzle is indistinct. The flame seems to 'bleed' into the metal guard rather than originating from a precise point source. The geometry of the metal wind guard is slightly soft and ill-defined.
The perspective of the flint wheel and the surrounding metal housing feels slightly inconsistent; the wheel appears almost 2D and flat against the more 3D-looking nozzle tube.
